svg.title: Customer Support AI Agent — detailed runtime flow
svg.desc: An implementation-based flow diagram covering the React interface, FastAPI request handling, deterministic intent routing, policy retrieval and generation, customer data tools, guarded cancellation, memory, escalation, JSON storage, policy ingestion, and evaluation.
svg.text: Detailed runtime flow • grounded in the repository implementation, not just the architecture proposal
React · FastAPI · Python · JSON demo store

text.tspan: Signs in, then submits a message.
UI holds chat state, conversation ID,
Input is validated; request ID is attached
Python keyword/ID rules choose the route.
and cancellation paths require a valid
No LLM chooses the operational route.

svg.text: 2 · Deterministic routing sends the message to a specialized path

text.tspan: source text; response cites source titles.
Refund, return, exchange, shipping, warranty and contact guidance go to RAG.
Greetings, clarifications and unrelated questions return direct deterministic replies.
If vector embedding is unavailable, BM25 can still find evidence; no valid evidence escalates.

svg.text: Ownership check → JSON repository → factual response

text.tspan: Order-backed tools verify the order belongs to the authenticated customer;
product/review tools query their own demo records. Missing/unavailable data is not reported as success.

svg.text: Mixed product + policy question → run product tool and RAG; return both parts.
Cancellation is a two-phase, explicit-consent process

text.tspan: Show optional reason in the UI.

svg.text: 4 · Server rechecks, then records an authoritative outcome

text.tspan: Revalidate token + customer + order version/eligibility; idempotency key protects retry handling.
Atomic repository update changes the order and cancellation history; expired/invalid requests are rejected.

svg.text: Outcomes: cancelled · declined · withdrawn · ineligible | Failures return explicit 401 / 409 / 503 responses.

text.tspan: Load using conversation ID + verified owner.
Can reuse the last order ID for a follow-up;
Keep up to 200 turns + first user message;
generation or unresolved billing issue can
create a local, redacted support ticket.
Return ticket ID + configured contact links;

svg.text: 4 · Policy knowledge is prepared separately, then used by the RAG route

text.tspan: chunking falls back to deterministic splits.
The docs describe agent routing, but chat currently uses deterministic Python rules; LangChain StructuredTools wrap the data functions.
Groq generates policy answers and semantic chunk proposals; Mistral provides embeddings. This is not an LLM autonomously selecting tools.

svg.text: Demo JSON repository (source of truth for this implementation)

text.tspan: Lookups return only records relevant to route.
Validated JSON reads/writes; data is fictional.

svg.text: Future MongoDB migration is documented, but runtime storage here is JSON (not MongoDB).
Errors are surfaced through FastAPI validation, HTTP error handlers and explicit unavailable responses.

text.tspan: Synthetic cases run through the same orchestrator.
Single case: answer, route, retrieval context, safe
tool trace, deterministic safety checks + metrics.
Dataset: filtered run queued in background; status
and results are persisted for later retrieval.
Cancellation preview is read-only during evaluation.
quality gate also checks deterministic safety outcomes.
ChatResponse: conversation_id · answer · route · source citations · UI actions · confirmation/support flags · memory diagnostics.
The React UI renders the answer, source titles, next action, cancellation controls or ticket/contact links; errors remain visible and retryable when safe.

svg.text: Tests cover routing · API · tools · RAG · memory · auth · cancellation · evaluation
Generated from tracked application code, data layout, tests and architecture documentation. Flow reflects the current demo implementation.
